channel.title: Biokineticum Blog
channel.description: Lab notes, telerehabilitation, and research explainers by Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler.

item.title: Side kick vs turning kick: what gender, height and weight actually change
item.description: Side kicks outscore turning kicks on a force plate (p<0.001). Gender, mass and height enter the model — some trained women still beat some men.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: What drives kicking strength in female taekwon-do athletes?
item.description: Five elite women, 100 kicks: side kick mean peak ~1770 N vs turning ~1379 N. Effective mass ~85% of body mass on the side kick.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: Kicking force: aggression, sex and age — what actually predicted
item.description: Pilot on 30 athletes: sex and age explained total kicking force (R²=0.53). BPAQ aggression was not a significant predictor.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: How much of your body mass actually arrives in a TKD kick?
item.description: Median force ~2662 N (turning) vs ~4596 N (side). Effective mass ~20% vs ~73% of body mass — technique, not scale weight.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: Men, women, and the effective mass of a taekwon-do kick
item.description: Nine black belts on plate + IMU: large force gaps between turning and side kicks; sex shapes how effective mass is utilised.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: Case studies: side kicks hit the plate harder than turning kicks
item.description: Four elite men, 80 kicks: side kick resultant ~4429 N vs turning ~2649 N. Left–right turning kicks similar.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: Not only the foot: core and arm velocities in the roundhouse kick
item.description: Thirteen elites kicking a table-tennis ball: sternum and opposite-shoulder max velocities differed by side; correlations with toe speed were side-specific.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: Cervicothoracic pain in nurses: trigger points beat classic massage
item.description: RCT in 24 women hospital staff: ischemic-compression trigger-point care outperformed classic massage on NDI, VAS and Laitinen scores.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: Facial nerve palsy: what six weeks of KT added to standard rehab
item.description: 27 patients (15 KT + standard rehab, 12 control): House-Brackmann −39.15% with KT vs −24.61% without.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: Effective distance: when peak punch velocity arrives too early
item.description: Black-belt case: punches 6.20–8.01 m/s. Best momentum transfer near 1.12–1.73% effective distance; later peaks nearly halved ball velocity.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: Same front kick, different targets: gender changes the answer
item.description: Vicon study: gender, leg and target all change front-kick speed (p<0.001). Men responded more to a board; women to a small ball.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: Forms are measurable: IMU diagnosis of saju-jirugi
item.description: Case study: fist IMUs during saju-jirugi. Striking punch max velocity fell 11.68→8.55 m/s; opposite hand retract peaked at 12.67 m/s (r=0.65).
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: Straight punches transfer more effective mass than hooks — even when hooks feel harder
item.description: 30 male boxers, four techniques: cross Me 31.17±16.20 kg, jab 30.39±15.09 kg; hooks ~12–14 kg despite higher fist acceleration.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: Is remote physiotherapy as good as in-person? What the reviews say
item.description: Systematic reviews find PT-led exercise telerehabilitation often non-inferior to face-to-face care for function, QoL and satisfaction — and how Biokineticum’s live PT + markerless model fits that frame.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: Markerless range of motion and balance from a home webcam
item.description: YOLOv8 on a home webcam for joint range of motion and a live sway map. Encrypted messengers, no LLM, 45 minutes from about 25 USD.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: One dataset from Biodex, Noraxon, Humac and force-plate PDFs
item.description: A native desktop tool that extracts Biodex, Noraxon, Humac and force-plate PDF/CSV reports into one multi-sensor dataset — local RAG, offline, GDPR-minded.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: High-g IMU strike diagnostics — and Perception Neuron 3 as the reference
item.description: Open high-g IMU hardware (up to 200 g) for combat-sport strikes, firmware and Python, next to Noitom Perception Neuron 3 as a portable reference system.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: PhysioSim: orthopaedic tests, imaging, and a diagnostic-accuracy report
item.description: A Telegram Mini App for physiotherapy students: history, Lasègue, Phalen, Tinel, Lachman, imaging, and an automatic diagnostic-accuracy report.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: How Hand and Trunk Movement Influences Kicking Power? Biomechanical Research in Taekwon-do
item.description: Did you know that a powerful roundhouse kick depends heavily on what your arms and trunk are doing? We tested 13 elite athletes in the laboratory to understand what optimizes energy transfer to the striking foot.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: Jab or Cross? What Determines the Power of a Knockout Punch in Boxing.
item.description: Higher speed doesn't always equal greater striking power. View the results of the latest biomechanical research on the differences between the lead hand (jab) and rear hand (cross) punch.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: Kicking in the Air vs a Target? Why Traditional Karate Training Requires Changes.
item.description: In traditional karate, we spend hundreds of hours executing techniques in the air. However, my latest research using EMG sensors exposes that the human body behaves entirely differently when it must hit a physical target.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: Effective Mass in Boxing. Why Heavy Weight Doesn't Guarantee a Knockout?
item.description: What exactly is 'effective mass' and why do you utilize a mere fraction of your body weight during a punch? A biomechanical analysis of mass transfer in boxing strikes.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: Artificial Intelligence in Combat Sports. How Neural Networks Predict Striking Power?
item.description: Is it actually possible to measure a kick's colossal force without exorbitant dynamometric platforms? The results of our newest research indicate that Machine Learning models (LSTM) can calculate strike power based solely on body movement.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: Does the Presence of a Target Affect Your Kicking Speed? Biomechanical Research in Taekwon-do
item.description: Most martial arts training relies on techniques performed in the air. However, my latest research proves that your body moves fastest only when it encounters physical resistance in the form of a target pad.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: Tradition vs. Sport. Which Version of the Roundhouse Kick is Faster?
item.description: Different competitions require different executions of techniques. We analyzed 180 roundhouse kicks performed by Taekwon-do masters to check the biomechanical differences between the traditional and sports execution.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: Algorithms Tracking Stress. What Determines Anxiety in Young Men?
item.description: Artificial intelligence helps us analyze not only movement but also the human psyche. See how we utilized machine learning algorithms to investigate anxiety and stress levels in crisis situations.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: The Price of Full Contact. Injury Analysis in Kyokushin Karate.
item.description: Kyokushin Karate is considered one of the toughest combat sports in the world. We analyzed the injury histories of 61 elite competitors to see what gets damaged most often on the mat and how to effectively prevent it.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: Virtual Reality (VR) in Physiotherapy. How Technology Protects Against Injuries?
item.description: VR headsets aren't just entertainment for gamers. Discover how we utilized virtual reality to study defense reactions and prevent dangerous falls, especially among the elderly.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: Taekwondo as Therapy. How Martial Arts Reduce Aggression?
item.description: Combat sports are often associated with aggression. However, our analysis proves that adapting Para Taekwondo rules can be a powerful tool in behavioral therapy for individuals with intellectual disabilities.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)

item.title: Can You Get Used to Pain? Pain Perception in Muay Thai.
item.description: Thai boxing is one of the most brutal striking sports. We tested the pain thresholds of professionals and amateurs to see if years of taking hits can "reprogram" the nervous system.
item.author: biokineticum@proton.me (Dr. hab. Dariusz Mosler)
